sentences.text:
Since both the appeals have arisen out of the same award dated 28.08.2015 passed by 1st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mahasamund (C.G.), in Claim Case No.58/2013 awarding compensation of Rs.3,95,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of application till its realization in favour of the claimants, they are being disposed of by this common judgment.
2.

entities.text: 1st Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mahasamund
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: MAC No.1499/2015 has been preferred by the claimants for enhancement of compensation and MAC No.217/2016 has been preferred by the driver/owner of the offending vehicle for exonerating him from the liability of payment of compensation.

3. The gist of claim before the Claims Tribunal, in brief, was that on 28.12.2012 at about 1:00 p.m,
when deceased Mahadev Yadav along with his brother Mahendra Yadav was going on his motorcycle bearing registration No.CG 06 K 7974 from Pithoura to Sankra Market, near Brinda Dhaba on National Highway No.53, respondent no.1 driving the offending vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration No.CG 04 JA 2785 rashly and negligently, dashed their motorcycle, as a result of which,
Mahadev Yadav Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19528 suffered grievous injuries on his body and died during the course of treatment at CHC Pithoura.

Upon report being made in this regard, crime was registered against Tusram Patel at PS Pithoura, District Mahasamund (CG).
4.
It is claimed that at the time of accident, deceased Mahadev Yadav was an unmarried boy of about 19 years.
He was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by selling chicken.
Due to the casual death of Mahadev Yadav, there is an irreparable loss to the appellant/claimants who are the parents of the deceased.
Therefore, the claimants preferred an application before the Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs. 29,50,000/-.

5. Learned Claims Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents available on record,
assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month i.e. Rs.36,000/- per annum.

Since the deceased was unmarried and the claimants are the parents of the deceased, 50% of the income was deducted towards personal expenses and after deduction, the amount comes to Rs. 18,000/- per annum.
Considering the fact that the deceased was unmarried, multiplier of 15 was applied as per the age of the parents of deceased and the total loss of dependency worked out to Rs.2,70,000/-.
In addition, Rs.25,000/- for funeral expenses and Rs.1,00,000/- for love and affection has been awarded.
Accordingly, the Claims Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.3,95,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of application till its realization, in favour of the claimants.

While passing the impugned award, the Tribunal has reached to the conclusion that from the evidence available on record it has been clearly established that the offending vehicle was being driven in violation of the insurance policy condition and therefore, the Insurance Company was exonerated from its liability and the liability of payment of compensation saddled upon Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19528 the driver/owner of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Now the appeal preferred by the claimants is being decided first.

6. Learned counsel for appellant/claimants submits that the multiplier of 15 held by the Tribunal considering the age of the parents of the deceased is improper and it should be 18 as per the age of the deceased.
He submits that the Tribunal has assessed the income of deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month which is not proper.
He submits that the income of deceased should have been assessed as per the minimum wages applicable at the relevant point of time.

He next submits that the Tribunal has erred in not considering future prospects while computing compensation as it failed to appreciate the fact that the deceased could have earned much more if he had not met with the accident.
He submits that the Tribunal has awarded lesser compensation under other heads which also needs to be enhanced suitably.
He further submits that though the insurance company has been exonerated, considering the beneficiary legislation of the Motor Vehicles Act, an order of pay and recovery should have been passed.
Hence, prays for allowing their appeal.

7. On the other hand, it has been argued on behalf of the counsel for respondents that in the facts and circumstances of case, the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper and requires no further enhancement.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.
In a motor accident claim case, what is important is that, the compensation to be awarded by the Courts/Tribunals should be just and proper compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.
It should neither be a meager amount of compensation nor a Bonanza.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19528 10.
Now this Court shall examine as to whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper compensation in the given facts and circumstances of the case.
In the case at hand, the accident occurred on 28.12.2012 and as per the notification by Labour Department, the minimum wages of an unskilled labour at that point of time was Rs.4646/-.

Hence,
considering the deceased to be an unskilled labour, his income is assessed at Rs.4646/- per month i.e. Rs. 55,752/- per annum, as minimum wages.

As per National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, after adding 40% towards future prospect i.e. Rs.
22300.8, the annual income comes to Rs.78052.8/-.

Thus, the total compensation is recomputed as  Rs.8,12,475/- from which after deduction of Rs.3,95,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal, the enhanced compensation would be Rs.4,17,475/-.

15. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/owner submits that the Claims Tribunal has erred in exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability as the vehicle was duly insured with the Insurance Company.

He submits that the vehicle was being operated with valid fitness and permit given by the transport authorities and the policy of the vehicle was issued by the Insurance Company after duly verifying the fitness and permit of the vehicle.
Therefore, prays for allowing the appeal of the driver/owner by exonerating him from the liability of payment of compensation.

16. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19528 Company submits that at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was being operated in violation of the insurance policy terms as the vehicle did not have a valid permit and fitness certificate.
Therefore, the impugned order passed by the Tribunal exonerating the Insurance company form its liability is just and proper and does not warrant any interference.

17. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
18.
Perusal of the record would show that learned Tribunal, in paragraphs 10 to 12 of the impugned order has discussed this issue in detail.

The Tribunal has held that the Insurance Company has led Tusram Patel vs Indal on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85206926/
4 the evidence of one Animesh Kumar Tandan posted as Assistant Grade in Regional Transport Officer, Raipur who has categorically stated that the offending vehicle did not have valid permit and fitness at the time of accident.

sentences.text: Learned Tribunal after close scrutiny of the documents brought on record regarding valid permit and fitness of the offending vehicle at the time of accident has reached to the conclusion that there was clear breach of policy condition and therefore exonerated the Insurance Company from its liability.
There is no material available on record perverse or contrary to the finding of the Tribunal.
Hence, this Court does not find any error of illegality in the conclusion arrived at by the Tribunal regarding exoneration of the Insurance Company from its liability.

19. So far as the prayer by claimants for issuing an order of "pay and recover" is concerned, in the present case, admittedly, the offending vehicle was insured with respondent no.2 but due to breach of policy condition, the insurance company has been exonerated.

However, considering the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh and Another Vs.
Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19528 and others reported in (2018) 7 SCC 558 ordering the insurance company to pay first and then recover and also taking note of the facts and circumstances of the present case, particularly the fact that at the time of accident the vehicle was insured with insurance company, it is directed that the insurance company shall first pay the amount of compensation awarded to the claimants and then recover the same from the owner/ driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 20. In the result, MAC No.1499/2015 is partly allowed.
The claimants shall be entitled for the enhanced amount of Rs.4,17,475/- in addition to what is already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of enhancement of the award till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the above extent.
21. MAC No.217/2016 preferred by the driver/owner
is hereby dismissed.
22. The Registry is directed to communicate the claimants in writing "the enhanced amount" in this appeal as against the award made by the Tribunal below.

The said communication be made in Hindi Deonagri language and the help of paralegal workers may be availed with a co-ordination of Secretary, Legal Aid of the concerned area wherein the claimants reside.
